transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon, thank you for calling S-Net Customer Support. You are speaking with Gavin. What can I look up for you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Gavin, my name is Theodora. I moved into my new flat two weeks ago on the fourth of October, and my S-Net Full Fibre home-move order has been delayed twice now, leaving me with zero internet for fourteen days!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, Theodora, give me your eight-digit S-Net account number and your date of birth so I can open the file on my screen.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My account number is 44091827, and my date of birth is the twelfth of May 1991. My home-move order reference is HM-88412.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, I have entered account 44091827 and order reference HM-88412. The status column on the screen says 'Order Held - Exception Code WL-09'.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Exception Code WL-09? Nobody has called or emailed me to explain what that means! I work remotely as a financial analyst and I have been forced to sit in a noisy coffee shop down the road for two whole weeks!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exception Code WL-09 is a wayleave and multi-dwelling unit routing hold generated by the external fibre survey team on the sixth of October.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Why would there be a survey hold on the sixth of October when I booked this home move a full month before my moving date?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: To see why the surveyor flagged WL-09 on HM-88412, I need to check the physical layout of the building, Theodora. What floor is your new flat on, and how many flats are in the building altogether?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am on the second floor—Flat 2B—and it is a Victorian terraced townhouse that was converted into six separate flats last year.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And inside your second-floor flat, have you checked the hallway utility cupboard and the living room skirting board to see if a white Openreach optical network terminal box is already mounted on the wall?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I looked in the hallway meter cupboard and behind the living room door on the day I moved in. There is only an old blank plastic faceplate with a draw-rope tied inside the conduit tube, no powered optical box.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: A draw-rope inside an empty sub-duct means the internal riser tubing was laid during the refurbishment, but the optical fibre cable has not been blown up from the ground floor. Is there a communal electrical or telecoms riser cupboard in the ground-floor entrance hall?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, under the ground-floor stairs next to the electric meters there is a locked timber cupboard, and the building management agent gave me the key code for it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Have you looked inside that ground-floor cupboard or on the front exterior brickwork by the basement lightwell to see if there is a grey Openreach Customer Splice Point box or a multi-port fibre distribution node?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: When I opened the ground-floor cupboard with the gas engineer last week, there was a grey Openreach box on the back wall with coiled black fibre cable hanging next to it, not plugged into the six plastic tubes going upstairs.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, that explains the technical state on order HM-88412. The coiled black cable is the external feeder from the street footway box, and the six plastic micro-ducts go up to the six flats.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: If the cable is already inside the ground-floor cupboard and the plastic tubes with draw-ropes go straight up to my hallway in Flat 2B, why hasn't an engineer come out to pull the fibre through?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me look at the surveyor's attachment from the sixth of October. It says the contractor needed to tack a splice manifold tray onto the communal wall inside that ground-floor cupboard.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, and why didn't they tack the tray onto the wall on the sixth of October when my installation was supposed to happen?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Wait while I open the legacy surveyor notes system to read the attachment.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, I have the surveyor attachment open now, Theodora. Because the ground-floor cupboard is common parts owned by the freeholder, Openreach's MDU team placed a statutory wayleave permission hold on the building.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: A statutory wayleave hold? The freeholder is Oakridge Estates and their office is literally three streets away! Did anyone from S-Net even contact Oakridge Estates?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The automated wayleave pack was sent by post to the registered Land Registry title holder on the ninth of October, and the system waits for a wet-ink or DocuSign signature before releasing the MDU splicing team.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sent by post to Land Registry on the ninth of October?! Meanwhile I am spending fifteen pounds a day on coffee and pastries just to sit on cafe Wi-Fi and my personal mobile hotspot data has completely run out!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: S-Net cannot override Openreach's legal wayleave requirement for drilling or fixing distribution manifolds in communal freeholder cupboards, Theodora.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am not asking you to break the law, Gavin! I am asking why nobody told me for two weeks, and why S-Net hasn't called the managing agent at Oakridge Estates when I gave their phone number and email on my original home-move form!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Where did you enter the managing agent's phone number when you submitted the move request on the fourth of September?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: In the 'Landlord / Building Manager Contact Details' box on the My S-Net home-move web form! I typed in Sarah Jenkins at Oakridge Estates with her direct landline and email!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Wait, let me look at the raw XML order payload that went across from the legacy home-move form.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Well? Is Sarah Jenkins's contact info in there or not?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Actually, before I can open the full MDU property record on the wholesale portal, I noticed I never took your full security check earlier—can you confirm the postcode and street address of the new flat, and your four-digit PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You are only verifying my address and PIN now, halfway through the call?! It is Flat 2B, 74 Clarendon Road, Bristol, BS6 7EY, and my PIN is 6104.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, BS6 7EY and 6104 are entered now. Looking at the wholesale MDU record for 74 Clarendon Road, the landlord contact field was truncated by the order bridge, so Openreach defaulted to posting a letter to the freeholder company secretary.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So it was S-Net's own order bridge software that chopped off my managing agent's details and caused this two-week delay!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Look, the home-move provisioning team handles wayleave delays and MDU order bridge exceptions, that's their department not mine, so you'll have to ring their desk tomorrow morning and get them to update the landlord contact.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait a second—you are telling me that after S-Net's system lost my building manager's details and left me without internet in Flat 2B for fourteen days, I have to call another department myself tomorrow morning?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I sit on the general customer support queue, Theodora. I only have read-only view on MDU wayleave exceptions under code WL-09, whereas the home-move provisioning desk owns the Openreach wayleave portal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Why can't you transfer me to the home-move provisioning desk right now or email them Sarah Jenkins's details on my behalf?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please bear with me while I check whether the home-move provisioning desk internal queue is taking transfers right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks for waiting, Theodora. The home-move provisioning back-office queue closed for inbound transfers at four o'clock, and they do not take internal emails from front-line agents.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: This is unbelievable. When I booked the move on the fourth of September, the sales agent promised me that because the street had Full Fibre, moving into 74 Clarendon Road on the fourth of October would be a seamless day-one activation!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Well, moving into a newly converted Victorian building and expecting fibre to magically appear on day one is a bit optimistic, isn't it?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Excuse me?! Did you seriously just call me 'a bit optimistic' for expecting the service I am paying for to work on the activation date S-Net confirmed in writing?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am simply pointing out that newly converted multi-dwelling Victorian properties almost always require secondary MDU splicing and freeholder wayleave sign-off before an ONT can be fitted.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Then S-Net's booking system should check that during the thirty days before I move in, instead of making snide remarks to me when I have been working out of a coffee shop for two weeks!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The automated availability checker only sees that the street cabinet and footway box on Clarendon Road are FTTP-enabled; it does not know whether the internal riser sub-ducts have been spliced until the engineer visits.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fine. Since my fibre line on order HM-88412 is still stuck in this WL-09 wayleave black hole, can you at least send me out a temporary 4G or 5G mobile broadband hub or add unlimited data to my mobile so I can work from my flat?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Temporary 4G backup dongles can only be dispatched by the home-move provisioning case handler once a confirmed installation date has been missed by more than ten working days on their tracker.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It HAS been fourteen calendar days since the fourth of October—that IS ten working days today!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because the order went into 'Customer/Landlord Wayleave Hold WL-09' on the sixth of October, the regulatory SLA clock is paused on the system, so my screen blocks me from ordering a 4G dongle.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Paused as a landlord hold because YOUR system truncated the landlord's contact details! Can you at least type Sarah Jenkins's phone number and email into the general account notes on HM-88412?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I can add a general notepad entry on account 44091827 for Sarah Jenkins at Oakridge Estates. Give me her phone number and email and I will type them into the scratchpad.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Her direct number at Oakridge Estates is 0117 496 0821, and her email is s.jenkins@oakridge-estates.co.uk.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have typed 'Sarah Jenkins, Oakridge Estates, 0117 496 0821, s.jenkins@oakridge-estates.co.uk' into the general account notepad against HM-88412.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will typing that into the general account notepad automatically alert the home-move provisioning team tomorrow morning?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, general notepad entries do not trigger a work-item wake-up in the provisioning queue, Theodora. You will still need to dial 0800 092 4410 after nine o'clock tomorrow morning and select option three for the home-move desk.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me write that down: 0800 092 4410, option three. And what am I supposed to ask them to do when I get through?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Tell the provisioning case handler to copy Sarah Jenkins's contact details from the general notepad into the Openreach MDU wayleave portal for 74 Clarendon Road so Openreach can email the DocuSign agreement.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And once Sarah Jenkins signs the DocuSign agreement for the ground-floor cupboard under the stairs, how long does it take to actually get an engineer to blow the fibre up the tube to Flat 2B?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Once Openreach receives the signed wayleave, their MDU build crew usually books the internal manifold splicing within five to seven working days, and then the final ONT installation inside Flat 2B is booked after that.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So I am looking at another week or two without home broadband even after the form is signed. Am I being billed the thirty-nine pounds a month while I have no service?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your monthly billing at 74 Clarendon Road does not start until the ONT inside Flat 2B passes its optical light test and order HM-88412 completes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Well, at least I am not paying monthly rental for thin air, though I will be claiming every penny of statutory delay compensation once this nightmare is over.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The provisioning team will calculate any applicable Ofcom automatic compensation once the WL-09 exception code is reviewed at order completion.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right. So nothing has actually been progressed today other than a note on my file and a phone number for me to ring tomorrow morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Everything from the surveyor attachment and the MDU wayleave process has been explained, and Sarah Jenkins's details are saved in the notepad on account 44091827.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fine, I will call the home-move desk myself at nine o'clock tomorrow morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, Theodora. Thank you for choosing S-Net, and goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.
